basis: Mood disorder; hypersomnia and subjective limb heaviness do not establish neurologic or muscle damage.
Familial atrial fibrillation is a cardiac rhythm disorder; no additional organ damage is established.
Defined by cutaneous manifestations of malignancy; an immune mechanism is not universal across this umbrella.
Chronic pericardial inflammation from immune-mediated rheumatic heart disease.
Inherited combined immunodeficiency; pneumonia, bronchitis and otitis are separately diagnosed infections, not intrinsic additional organ disease.
Intrinsic sweat-gland dysfunction causes generalized anhidrosis in 5/5 patients despite normal gland anatomy.
Primary skin eruption caused by sweat-duct obstruction; no additional organ involvement.
Lymphokine immunodeficiency with persistent Candida infection of skin, nails and mucosa, especially oral mucosa.
Isolated unilateral absence or hypoplasia of central hand bones and digits; development otherwise normal.
Titin-related myopathy affects skeletal muscle; the neuromuscular parent does not establish nerve disease. Cardiac involvement varies by subtype.
Malignant bone-forming tumour arising on the bone surface; metastatic sites are not intrinsic primary organs.
Inherited type I interferon-mediated inflammation; AGS-like damaging encephalopathy is the predominant presentation (>30%).
Congenital skeletal reduction defect with a single digit on each limb; typically isolated.
Hereditary essential tremor is a neurologic movement disorder; vocal tremor does not establish airway disease.
Inherited calcium-sensing disorder causes hypercalcemia and hypocalciuria; low urinary calcium is not kidney damage. Stones and pancreatitis are uncommon separate diseases.
Childhood malignant embryonal tumour originating in the cerebellum.
Frontonasal skeletal/nasal malformation; damaging eye and CNS defects frequent (30-79%). Oral clefts and hearing impairment also frequent, omitted at cap.
Developmental delay, lung cysts and Wilms tumour define GLOW; kyphosis and pectus excavatum each reported in 1/2 patients, supporting skeletal involvement.
Muscular dystrophy, chronic respiratory insufficiency (4/4) and skin abnormalities define the syndrome; motor delay reflects muscle weakness.
Excess endolymph distorts cochlear and vestibular structures, causing hearing loss and vestibular dysfunction.
Congenital absence of normal eyelids and palpebral fissures; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Inherited early-onset seizure disorder with intellectual disability and myoclonus.
Digital phalangeal hypoplasia defines disease; developmental speech/language delay reported in 1/2 patients (50%), with limited precision from the small cohort.
NANS-related sialic-acid biosynthesis disorder defined by skeletal dysplasia and severe developmental/intellectual impairment; cerebral atrophy in 4/6.
Metabolic lipodystrophy, cataracts and neurodegeneration define syndrome; subcutaneous fat loss in 4/5. Vascular/pleural findings omitted at cap; pancreatitis is separate.
